checks.cmd: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$o = @(Get-Content work/term-06/order.txt | Where-Object { $_.Trim() -ne '' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() }); if ($o.Count -ne 5) { exit 1 }; if ($o[0] -ne 'build') { exit 1 }; if ($o[-1] -ne 'deploy') { exit 1 }; $p = @{}; for ($i = 0; $i -lt $o.Count; $i++) { $p[$o[$i]] = $i }; if ($p.Count -ne 5) { exit 1 }; if ($p['test'] -le $p['build']) { exit 1 }; if ($p['lint'] -le $p['build']) { exit 1 }; if ($p['package'] -le $p['test']) { exit 1 }; if ($p['package'] -le $p['lint']) { exit 1 }; if ($p['deploy'] -le $p['package']) { exit 1 }; exit 0"

description: Harder: topological sort of a dependency file.
prompt: Read work/term-06/deps.txt. Each non-blank, non-comment line has the form "<node>: <space-separated deps>" meaning the node depends on the listed deps (a node with nothing after the colon has no deps). Lines starting with "#" and blank lines must be ignored. Compute a valid topological order (every dependency appears BEFORE the node that depends on it) and write one node per line to work/term-06/order.txt with no blank lines and no extra text. Every node from the input must appear exactly once. Hint: python one-liner/script with stdlib only, or PowerShell. No network, no installs.

setupFiles.content:
# term-06 dependency graph: '<node>: <space-separated deps>' means node depends on deps
build:
test: build
lint: build
package: test lint
deploy: package

title: Topological sort
